x: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Commentary on Sūrat "Idhā zulzilat" [al-Zalzala]
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted, majestic is His majesty and hallowed His names:

When the earth is shaken with its quaking (1) and the earth brings out its burdens (2) and man says: What is the matter with it? (3) That Day it will report its news (4) because your Lord has inspired it (5) That Day the people will proceed in separate groups to be shown their deeds (6) So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7) and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it (8)
He, exalted be His mention, says:
at the coming of the Hour,
, so that it is convulsed violently.
, is a verbal noun, and with a
is annexed to the earth although it is its attribute, as one says: "I will honor you with your honoring," meaning: "I will honor you with an honoring." This is fitting in
because it agrees with the rest (1) of the verse-endings that follow it.

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yamān told us, from Ashʿath, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿīd, he said:
m: The earth quaked in the time of ʿAbd Allāh, and ʿAbd Allāh said to it: "What is the matter with you? Had it spoken, the Hour would have come."

x: and the earth brings out its burdens
. He says: the earth brings out what is in its belly of the dead, alive. The dead person in the belly of the earth is a burden to it, and when he is alive on its surface he is a burden upon it.
The people of interpretation said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:
Muḥammad b. Sinān al-Qazzāz told me, he said:

c: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, from Shabīb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: h
and the earth brings out its burdens
. He said: the dead (1).

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: h
and the earth brings out its burdens
. He said: he means the dead.

c: Al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both (2) from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
h
and the earth brings out its burdens
: those who are in the graves (3).

x: and man says: What is the matter with it?
. He, exalted be His mention, says: and the people say, when the earth is shaken at the coming of the Hour: what is the matter with the earth (4), and what is its story?
That Day it will report its news

c: Ibn ʿAbbās used to say about this what Ibn Sinān al-Qazzāz told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, from Shabīb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: h
and man says: What is the matter with it?
. He said: the disbeliever;
h
That Day it will report its news

. He says: that Day the earth will report its news (1) and its reporting its news, on the view that we mentioned from ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd, is that it will speak and say: "God commanded me this, and inspired me to it, and permitted me in it." As for Saʿīd b. Jubayr, he used to say about this what Abū Kurayb told us, he said:

c: Wakīʿ told us, from Ismāʿīl b.
m: ʿAbd al-Malik, he said: I heard Saʿīd b. Jubayr reciting (1) in the evening prayer once: (
i
yawmaʾidhin tunbiʾu akhbārahā
), and another time:
h
i
tuḥaddithu akhbārahā
(2). So the meaning of
h
i
tuḥaddithu
in Saʿīd's view was:
i
tunbiʾu

(3) ("it informs"). And its informing of its news is its bringing out its burdens from its belly to its surface. In my view this is a view with a sound meaning. The interpretation of the statement on this meaning is: that Day the earth will make its news plain by the quaking and convulsion and the bringing out of the dead from its bellies to its surface, by God's inspiring it and His permission to it to do so. That is the meaning of His saying:
h
because your Lord has inspired it

x: The people of interpretation said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:
Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said:

c: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us;
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding the saying of God:
h
and the earth brings out its burdens
: he says (4):
h
your Lord has inspired it
. He said: He commanded it, and it cast out what was in it and emptied itself.

c: Al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
m: h
because your Lord has inspired it
. He said: He commanded it (1). It has also been reported that ʿAbd Allāh used to recite it: (
i
yawmaʾidhin tunabbaʾu
i
akhbārahā
) (3). And it was said: its meaning is that the earth will report its news of those who were on its surface, the people of obedience and of disobedience, and what good or evil they did upon it.
i
Mention of those who said this:
Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said:

c: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān:
m: h
That Day it will report its news
. He said: What good or evil was done upon it;
h
because your Lord has inspired it
. He said: He made it know that.

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His saying:
h
That Day it will report its news
. He said: What was in it and on its surface of the deeds of the servants.

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us;
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying:
h
That Day it will report its news
. He said: It informs the people of what they did upon it (1). And it was said: by His saying
h
has inspired it
is meant: has inspired to it.
i
Mention of those who said this:
Ibn Sinān al-Qazzāz told me, he said:

c: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, from Shabīb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: h
has inspired it
. He said: has inspired to it (1).

evidence.text: It has also been reported that ʿAbd Allāh used to recite it: (*yawmaʾidhin tunabbaʾu* (2) *akhbārahā*) (3).

x: That Day the people will proceed in separate groups
. It was said that this phrase belongs later, after

. They said: the order of the speech is: that Day it will report its news because your Lord has inspired it, to be shown their deeds; that Day the people will proceed in separate groups. They said: but this phrase was interposed between them. The meaning of His saying
That Day the people will proceed in separate groups
is: that Day the people will go forth from the place of reckoning in separate bands, some taking the right side to Paradise and others taking the left side to the Fire.

. He says: that Day the people will proceed in separate groups, divided, to the right and to the left, to be shown their deeds. The doer of good in the world, obedient to God, will see his deed and what God has prepared for him on that day of honor for his obedience to Him in the world; and the wrongdoer, disobedient to God, will see his deed and the recompense of his deed, and what God has prepared for him of humiliation and disgrace in Hell for his disobedience to Him in the world and his disbelief in Him.
So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it
. He says: whoever did in the world the weight of a speck (
) of good will see its reward there;
and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it
. The Exalted says: and whoever did in the world the weight of a speck of evil will see its recompense there. It was said:

, though the report about it concerns the Hereafter, because the hearer understands the meaning of this, given the evidence that preceded earlier that its meaning is: "whoever did." That is indicated by His saying
That Day the people will proceed in separate groups to be shown their deeds
. But since the meaning of the speech was understood by the hearers, and since in His saying

there is an exhortation to the people of the world to act in obedience to God and a deterrent from disobeying Him, together with what I mentioned of the evidence of the speech before that, that it is intended as a report of their past deeds and what is due to them for them, the report was brought out (1) in the form of a report about future action.
The people of interpretation said the same as we have said, that all of them will see their deeds.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: regarding His saying:
h
So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it

. He said: There is no believer and no disbeliever who did good or evil in the world but God will bring it to him. As for the believer, He will show him his good deeds and his evil deeds, and God will forgive him his evil deeds; and as for the disbeliever, He will reject his good deeds and punish him for his evil deeds (2). Something other than this was also said about it.

x: Some of them said: as for the believer, the punishment of his evil deeds is hastened for him in the world and the reward of his good deeds is deferred for him, while for the disbeliever the reward of his good deeds is hastened and the punishment of his evil deeds is deferred.
Mention of those who said this:
Mūsā b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Masrūqī told me, he said:

c: Muḥammad b. Bashr told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Muslim al-Ṭāʾifī told me
m: it, from ʿAmr b. Qatāda, he said: I heard Muḥammad b. Kaʿb al-Qurẓī interpreting this verse:
h
So (1) whoever does an atom's weight

. He said: Whoever does an atom's weight of good, being a disbeliever, will see its reward in the world, in himself, his family, his wealth and his children, until he leaves the world and has no good with Him;
h
and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it

, being a believer, will see its punishment in the world, in himself, his family, his wealth and his children, until he leaves the world and has nothing (against him) with Him (2). Maḥmūd (3) b. Khidāsh told me, he said:

c: Muḥammad b. Yazīd al-Wāsiṭī told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Muslim al-Ṭāʾifī told us, from ʿAmr b.
m: Dīnār, he said: I asked Muḥammad b. Kaʿb al-Qurẓī about this verse:
h
So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7) and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it

. He said: Whoever does an atom's weight of good, being a disbeliever, will see its reward in himself, his family and his wealth, until he leaves (4) and has no good; and whoever does an atom's weight of evil, being a believer, will see its punishment in himself, his family and his wealth (5), until he leaves and has no evil.

c: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb al-Ḥassānī told me, he said: al-Haytham b. al-Rabīʿ told us, he said: Simāk b. ʿAṭiyya told us, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilāba, from Anas, he said:
m: Abū Bakr ؓ was eating with the Prophet ﷺ when this verse was revealed:
h
So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7) and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it

. Abū Bakr raised his hand (6) and said: O Messenger of God, am I to be recompensed for what I did of an atom's weight of evil? He said: "O Abū Bakr, whatever you see in the world of what you dislike is the weights (1) of motes of evil, and God stores up for you the weights of motes of good until you are given it in full on the Day of Resurrection" (2).

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, [he said: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb told us
m: ] (3), he said: Ayyūb told us, he said: We found in the book of Abū Qilāba, from Abū Idrīs, that Abū Bakr was eating with the Prophet ﷺ when this verse was revealed:
h
So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7) and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it

. He said: Abū Bakr lifted his hand from the food and said: "Shall I see what I did?" He said: I know only that he said: what I did (4) of good and evil. The Prophet ﷺ said: "What you see of what you dislike is the weights of motes of much evil, and God stores up for you the weights of motes of good until it is given to you on the Day of Resurrection." And the confirmation of that is in the Book of God:
h
And whatever strikes you of disaster is for what your hands have earned; and He pardons much

c: Yaʿqūb told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, he said: Ayyūb told us, he said:
m: I read in the book of Abū Qilāba, he said: There was revealed:
h
So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7) and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it

, while Abū Bakr was eating (6); he stopped and said: O Messenger of God, I will see what I did of good or (1) evil? He said: "Have you seen what you have seen of what you dislike? It is from the weights of motes of evil, and the weights of motes of good are stored up until you are given them on the Day of Resurrection." Abū Idrīs said: I see its confirmation in the Book of God, He said:
h
And whatever strikes you of disaster is for what your hands have earned; and He pardons much

c: Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Dāwūd, from al-Shaʿbī, he said: ʿĀʾisha said:
m: O Messenger of God, ʿAbd Allāh b. Judʿān used to maintain family ties and do this and that; will that benefit him? He said: "No; he never said one day: My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment."

c: Ibn Wakīʿ told us, he said: Ḥafṣ told us, from Dāwūd, from al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾisha, she said:
m: I said: O Messenger of God, Ibn Judʿān in the Jāhiliyya used to maintain family ties and feed the poor; will that benefit him? He said: "It will not benefit him; he never said one day: My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment" (3).

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī told us, from Dāwūd, from ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī,
m: that ʿĀʾisha, Mother of the Believers, said: O Messenger of God, ʿAbd Allāh b. Judʿān used to maintain family ties, entertain the guest and free the captive; will that benefit him at all? He said: "No; he never said one day: My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment."

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī told us, from Dāwūd, from ʿĀmir,
m: from (4) ʿAlqama, that Salama b. Yazīd al-Juʿfī said: O Messenger of God, our mother died in the Jāhiliyya; she used to maintain family ties, entertain the guest, and do this and that; will that benefit her at all? He said: "No" (1).

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: al-Ḥajjāj b. al-Minhāl told us, he said: al-Muʿtamir b. Sulaymān told us, he said: Dāwūd told us, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAlqama b.
m: Qays, from Salama b. Yazīd al-Juʿfī, he said: My brother and I went to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and I said: O Messenger of God, our mother in the Jāhiliyya used to entertain the guest and maintain family ties; will her deed benefit her at all? He said: "No" (2).

c: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Ṣudrān and Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told me,
m: both saying: al-Muʿtamir b. Sulaymān told us, he said: Dāwūd b. Abī Hind told us, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAlqama, from Salama b. Yazīd, from the Prophet ﷺ, similarly.
b.via: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Ṣudrān and Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from [ʿAmr b.
m: ] (3) Qatāda, from Muḥammad b. Kaʿb, that he said: As for the believer, he will see his good deeds in the Hereafter, and as for the disbeliever, he will see his good deeds in the world (4).

c: Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: Abū Naʿāma told us, he said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Bushayr al-Ḍabbī told us
m: — his grandfather was Salmān (5) b. ʿĀmir — that Salmān (5) b. ʿĀmir came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: My father used to maintain family ties, keep his covenants and honor the guest. He said: "Did he die before Islam?" He said: Yes. He said: "That will not benefit him." Then he turned away, and the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Bring the old man to me." He came, and the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "It will not benefit him, but it will be among his descendants, and they will never be disgraced, never be humbled, and never be impoverished" (1).

c: Ibn al-Muthannā and Ibn Bashshār told us,
m: both saying: Abū Dāwūd told us, he said: ʿImrān told us, from Qatāda, from Anas, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "God does not wrong a believer in a single good deed: he is rewarded for it with provision in the world and recompensed for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, He gives to him for it in the world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes he has no good deed" (2).

c: Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, he said: Layth told us, he said: al-Muʿallā told me, from Muḥammad b.
m: Kaʿb al-Qurẓī, he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "No doer of good, believer or disbeliever, does good but its reward falls upon God, either in his immediate world or in his later Hereafter" (3).

c: Yūnus b. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: [Ḥuyayy (4) b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū ʿAbd] (5) al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī (6) informed me, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ, that he said: (7)
h
When the earth is shaken with its quaking

was revealed while Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq was sitting. He wept when it was revealed, and the Messenger of God ﷺ said to him: "What makes you weep, O Abū Bakr?" He said: This sūra makes me weep. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "If you did not err and sin, so that God forgives you, God would create a people who would err and sin, and He would forgive them" (1). These reports from the Messenger of God ﷺ inform that the believer sees the punishment of his evil deeds in the world and the reward of his good deeds in the Hereafter, and that the disbeliever sees the reward of his good deeds in the world and the punishment of his evil deeds in the Hereafter, and that the benefit of the good done in the world before it does not reach the disbeliever in the Hereafter, along with his disbelief.

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn ʿAlī told us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, he said:
m: I met seventy of the Companions of ʿAbd Allāh, the youngest of whom was al-Ḥārith b. Suwayd, and I heard him reciting:
h
When the earth is shaken with its quaking
until he reached:
h
So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7) and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it
. He said: This is a severe reckoning (2). It was also said that the
i
dharra
is a red worm that has no weight.
i
Mention of those who said this:
Isḥāq b. Wahb al-ʿAllāf and Muḥammad b. Sinān al-Qazzāz told me, both saying:

c: Abū ʿĀṣim told us.
m: He said: Shabīb b. Bishr told us, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying:
h
the weight of a
i
dharra
. Ibn Sinān said in his report: the weight of a red
i
dharra
. Ibn Wahb said in his report: a red ant. Isḥāq said: Yazīd b. Hārūn said: They claim that this red worm has no weight (3). End of the commentary on Sūrat "al-Zalzala"

notes.en: Manuscripts M and T1 omit it.
Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/380) to the author, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور 6/ 380 إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه.

notes.en: This is how it appears in the manuscripts; the correct text omits it.
Tafsir Mujahid, p. 742. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/380) to al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 742، وعزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور 6/ 380 إلى الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Manuscripts S and T3 read “al-ard” (“the earth”).
Manuscripts T2 and T3 read “yaqulu” (“he says”).

Ibn Abi Shayba transmitted it in his Musannaf (1/358) from Wakiʿ. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/380) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif. The reading “tunabbiʾu” is anomalous; see Mukhtasar Shawadh al-Qurʾan by Ibn Khalawayh (p. 177).
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة في مصنفه 1/ 358 عن وكيع به، وعزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور 6/ 380، إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن الأنبارى في المصاحف. وقراءة (تنبئ) شاذة. ينظر مختصر الشواذ لابن خالويه ص 177.

notes.en: Manuscripts T1, T2, and T3 read “tabayyan.”
Manuscript M reads “bi-an” (“that”).
The source references were given earlier on p. 559.
Manuscripts T2 and T3 read “tabayyan.”
See al-Farraʾ, Maʿani al-Qurʾan (3/284).
The source references were given earlier on p. 559.
Manuscripts S, T1, T2, and T3 read “ikhraj” (“bringing forth”).
Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Baʿth (no. 59) through Abu Salih with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/381) to Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقى في البعث (59) من طريق أبي صالح به، وعزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور 6/ 381 إلى ابن المنذر.

notes.en: Manuscripts S, T1, T2, and T3 read “min” (“from”).
ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/388) from Maʿmar, from ʿAmr ibn Qatadah. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/381) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 388 عن معمر، عن عمرو بن قتادة به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 381 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Manuscripts T2 and T3 read “Muhammad.” See al-Jarh wa-l-Taʿdil (8/291).
notes.ar: في ت 2، ت 3: "محمد". وينظر الجرح والتعديل 8/ 291.

notes.en: Manuscript M adds “min al-dunya” (“from the world”) after it.
Manuscripts T2 and T3 add “wa-waladuhu” (“and his child”) after it.
Manuscript M adds “min al-taʿam” (“of food”) after it.
Manuscripts M, T2, and T3 read “fa-mithqala.”

Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/484) from the author. Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted it in his Tafsir—as cited in Ibn Kathir’s Tafsir—and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (no. 8407) through Abu al-Khattab Ziyad ibn Yahya. Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Shuʿab (no. 9808) through al-Haytham ibn al-Rabiʿ. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/380) to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Hakim in his Tarikh. The source references were also given earlier at 20/513.
notes.ar: ذكرُه ابنُ كثير في تفسيره 8/ 484 عن المصنف، وأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره - كما في تفسير ابن كثير - والطبراني في الأوسط (8407) مِن طريق أبي الخطاب زياد بن يحيى به، وأخرجه البيهقي في الشعب (9808) مِن طريق الهيثم بن الربيع به، وعزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور 6/ 380 إلى ابن المنذر وابن مردويه والحاكم في تاريخه، وتقدم تخريجه 20/ 513.

notes.en: Manuscript M omits it.
Manuscript T2 reads “ʿalimti” (“you knew”).
Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/484) from the author. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/381) to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: ذكرُه ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 484 عن المصنف، وعزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور 6/ 381 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: Manuscript M adds “with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him” after it.
notes.ar: بعده في م: "مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ".

notes.en: Manuscripts M and T1 add “wa” (“and”) after it.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/484) from the author; it was also cited earlier at 20/513.
notes.ar: ذكرُه ابنُ كثير في تفسيره 8/ 484 عن المصنف، وتقدم في 20/ 513.

notes.en: Ahmad (6/93, al-Maymaniyya edition), Muslim (no. 214), and Ibn Hibban (no. 331) transmitted it through Hafs ibn Ghiyath.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 6/ 93 (الميمنية)، ومسلم (214)، وابن حبان (331) من طريق حفص بن غياث به.

notes.en: Manuscripts S, T1, T2, and T3 read “ibn.”
Ahmad transmitted it (25/268, no. 15923) from Ibn Abi ʿAdi with this chain.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 25/ 268 (15923) عن ابن أبي عدى به.

notes.en: Al-Nasaʾi transmitted it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 11649) from Ibn al-Muthanna. Al-Tabarani (no. 6319) transmitted it through al-Hajjaj; al-Bukhari in his Tarikh (4/72) through Muʿtamir; and Ibn Abi ʿAsim in al-Ahad wa-l-Mathani (no. 2474) through Dawud.
notes.ar: أخرجه النسائي في الكبرى (11649) عن ابن المثنى به، وأخرجه الطبراني (6319) من طريق الحجاج به، وأخرجه البخارى في تاريخه 4/ 72 من طريق معتمر به، وأخرجه ابنُ أبي عاصم في الآحاد والمثاني (2474) مِن طريق داود به.

notes.en: The manuscripts omit it; it is restored from ʿAbd al-Razzaq’s Tafsir. See also p. 564.
notes.ar: سقط من النسخ، والمثبت مِن تفسير عبد الرزاق، وتقدم في ص 564.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/388) from Maʿmar with this chain.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 388 عن معمر به.

notes.en: Manuscripts S, T1, T2, and T3 read “Sulayman.” See Tahdhib al-Kamal (18/115).
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "سليمان"، وينظر تهذيب الكمال 18/ 115.

notes.en: Al-Tabarani transmitted it in al-Kabir (no. 6213) through Abu ʿAsim with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/382) to the author.
notes.ar: أخرجه الطبراني في الكبير (6213) من طريق أبي عاصم به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 382 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Al-Tayalisi transmitted it (no. 2123) from ʿImran with this chain; see the earlier discussion at 7/30.
notes.ar: أخرجه الطيالسي (2123) عن عمران به، وتقدم تخريجه في 7/ 30.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in al-Musannaf (no. 5200) through Layth; see the earlier discussion at 12/349.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في مصنفه (5200) من طريق ليث به، وينظر ما تقدم في 12/ 349.

notes.en: Manuscript M reads “Yahya.” See Tahdhib al-Kamal (7/488).
Manuscript T2 reads “Ibn ʿAbdullah.”
Manuscripts T1 and T2 read “al-Jili”; another T2 reading is “al-Jabali.”
Manuscripts S, T2, and T3 omit it.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya transmitted it in al-Riqqa wa-l-Bukaʾ (no. 75), al-Tabarani (no. 87; part of volume 13), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab (no. 7103) through several chains from Ibn Wahb. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/380) to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي الدنيا في الرقة والبكاء (75)، والطبراني (87) - قطعة مِن الجزء 13 - والبيهقي في الشعب (7103) مِن طرق عن ابن وهب به، وعزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور 6/ 380 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: Abu Nuʿaym transmitted it in Hilyat al-Awliyaʾ (4/127) through Abu Kurayb. Ibn Abi Shayba (14/11), Ibn Abi al-Dunya in al-Riqqa wa-l-Bukaʾ (no. 89), and Abu Nuʿaym in Hilyat al-Awliyaʾ (4/127) transmitted it through al-Aʿmash.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو نعيم في الحلية 4/ 127 مِن طريق أبى كريب، وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 14/ 11، وابن أبي الدنيا في الرقة والبكاء (89)، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 4/ 127 من طريق الأعمش به.

notes.en: The source references were given earlier at 7/29–30.
